The '''Detailed Surface Scanner''' ('''DSS''') is an optional internal module used to scan planets, moons, rings, and other bodies within a system, revealing surface detail, geological and biological signal counts, and other body-specific information used for exploration data value and site-hunting.

== Overview ==

Firing a Detailed Surface Scanner probe at a body — commonly called "honking" a body once mapped — reveals a fuller data set about it than the system-wide discovery scan alone provides, and is a prerequisite for locating specific surface points of interest. It is distinct from [[Sensors]], the core internal module governing general contact detection range.
